executiveSummary.assessed: Harborline Member Services Platform (fictional), operated by Meridian Commons Cooperative (fictional), assessed against the ten controls of Republika Sovereignty Assessment (rn.sv@0.1.0) with evidence up to 2026-05-31T00:00:00.000Z.
executiveSummary.purpose: Founding assessment of the platform’s digital-sovereignty posture before onboarding new member organizations.
principalRisks: SV-03: Decisions taken outside the declared policy.
SV-06: One organization reading or altering another organization’s data.
SV-10: No one accountable for sovereignty decisions.
nextActions: F-01: corrective action for SV-06 (Immediate priority).
F-02: corrective action for SV-03 (Normal priority).
F-03: provide evidence for SV-07 (Low priority).
F-04: provide evidence for SV-09 (Low priority).
F-05: corrective action for SV-10 (Low priority).

scope.systemDescription: A synthetic multi-tenant platform through which member organizations manage consent, service requests and payouts. Invented for this example.
dependencies: Managed identity provider operated by a third party
accessLimitations: Evidence was provided by the cooperative; no direct access to production systems was granted.
scope.periodFrom: Not specified (evidence up to the cutoff was considered)

Independent collection of evidence from the assessed systems: evidence was supplied by the assessed organization.

steps: Scope declared and fixed in the assessment record before evaluation (immutable scope).
The ten rn.sv@0.1.0 controls identified for the scope.
Evidence references collected; each manually supplied reference is bound to the requirement it was offered for.
Structural and provenance checks available to the Host applied: binding, tenant attribution, digests where present. Supplier claims of verification are recorded as claims only.
Each control reviewed by an authenticated reviewer holding the required role; a definitive conclusion must cite evidence accepted for that control.
Controls evaluated and scored under the framework methodology.
Findings derived and classified by rule-based severity.
Assessment integrity and finding histories verified.
This report generated deterministically from the verified assessment.
Release reviewed and approved by an authenticated human approver before delivery.
methodology.scoring: rn.sv.scoring@0.1.0: pass = 1, partial = 0.5, fail = 0; unknown and pending reviews score 0 and stay in the denominator; domain-weighted; a failed SV-06 or SV-08 marks its domain unhealthy.

controls.title: Actor identity and authority
controls.objective: Demonstrate that privileged operations are performed only by identified actors with authority in force.
controls.conclusion: The reviewer concluded the control's criteria were met over the reviewed sample: Every sampled privileged action maps to a unique identity holding authority in force at the time.
limitations: Sample-based: conclusions cover the sampled actions only.
Legitimate service accounts can look like shared accounts without their inventory.

controls.title: Consent and revocation
controls.objective: Demonstrate that data subjects’ consent decisions are recorded and honored, including withdrawal.
controls.conclusion: The reviewer concluded the control's criteria were met over the reviewed sample: Every sampled operation relied on consent in force and no operation followed a sampled revocation.
limitations: Consent captured outside the system may be invisible to the sample.

controls.title: Policy compliance
controls.objective: Demonstrate that the declared policy is the policy actually applied.
controls.conclusion: The reviewer concluded the criteria were met only in part over the reviewed sample.
limitations: Exceptions approved outside the tooling may appear as inconsistencies.
controls.revalidation: A new decision sample under the corrected policy version.

controls.title: Evidence integrity
controls.objective: Demonstrate that recorded evidence cannot be altered without detection.
controls.conclusion: The reviewer concluded the control's criteria were met over the reviewed sample: An integrity mechanism covers the critical records and verification succeeds over the sample.
limitations: Integrity is not truthfulness: a record that was false when written verifies as intact.
Without signatures, a privileged writer can recompute digests consistently.

controls.title: Execution traceability
controls.objective: Demonstrate that what was authorized can be connected to what actually happened.
controls.conclusion: The reviewer concluded the control's criteria were met over the reviewed sample: Each sampled operation is reconstructable from request to observed outcome.
limitations: Relies on the customer’s logs; log completeness is not independently established.

controls.title: Isolation between organizations
controls.objective: Demonstrate that one organization cannot read or alter another organization’s data.
controls.conclusion: The reviewer observed the control not satisfied: A cross-organization read or write succeeded, or an in-scope path does not enforce the organization scope.
limitations: This framework performs no active testing against customer systems; active testing requires separate written authorization and is out of scope for 0.1.0.
Legitimate global administrative roles cross organizations by design.
controls.revalidation: Re-execution of the isolation tests after the correction, witnessed or recorded.

controls.title: Minimal disclosure
controls.objective: Demonstrate that the platform discloses no more than each audience requires.
controls.conclusion: Not determined: the evidence available did not allow a defensible conclusion. This is an evidence gap, not an observed failure. Typical cause: No field inventory or samples were provided.
limitations: Field-level review only; no automated detection of personal data by value.
controls.revalidation: A new export sample after the correction.

controls.title: Effective revocation of authority
controls.objective: Demonstrate that revocation is effective in practice, not only recorded.
controls.conclusion: The reviewer concluded the control's criteria were met over the reviewed sample: The first attempt after revocation was denied within the documented bound.
limitations: This framework performs no active testing against customer systems; the test is executed by the customer in staging.
Caches with a documented time-to-live can delay denial legitimately.

controls.title: Remediation and revalidation
controls.objective: Demonstrate that the organization corrects issues and confirms the corrections.
controls.conclusion: Not determined: the evidence available did not allow a defensible conclusion. This is an evidence gap, not an observed failure. Typical cause: No tracking records were provided.
limitations: On a first assessment there may be no prior findings to sample.
controls.revalidation: Review of closures made after the correction date.

controls.title: Governance and accountability
controls.objective: Demonstrate that someone is accountable for sovereignty decisions and that the posture is reviewed.
controls.conclusion: The reviewer concluded the criteria were met only in part over the reviewed sample.
limitations: Documentary: the existence of a process does not prove its effectiveness.
controls.revalidation: Evidence of the next scheduled review after the correction.

results.interpretation: The score summarizes this framework’s methodology over the declared scope. A high score is not demonstrated sovereignty, and an UNKNOWN control lowers the score without being a failure. Read every control result and its limitations.
blockingRisks: SV-06 failed: the Data Boundaries domain is marked unhealthy regardless of its numeric score.

findings.label: F-01
findings.description: The reviewer observed the control not satisfied: A cross-organization read or write succeeded, or an in-scope path does not enforce the organization scope.
findings.risk: One organization reading or altering another organization’s data.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the tenant scope on every read and write path and cover it with automated isolation tests.
findings.closureCriterion: Re-execution of the isolation tests after the correction, witnessed or recorded.

findings.label: F-02
findings.description: The reviewer concluded the criteria were met only in part over the reviewed sample.
findings.risk: Decisions taken outside the declared policy.
findings.recommendation: Version the policy, record which version each decision used, and route exceptions through an attributable approval.
findings.closureCriterion: A new decision sample under the corrected policy version.

findings.label: F-03
findings.description: Not determined: the evidence available did not allow a defensible conclusion. This is an evidence gap, not an observed failure. Typical cause: No field inventory or samples were provided.
findings.recommendation: Provide the evidence the control requires so it can be concluded. If a gap is then confirmed: Define per-audience disclosure profiles and strip every field an audience does not need.
findings.closureCriterion: A new export sample after the correction.

findings.label: F-04
findings.description: Not determined: the evidence available did not allow a defensible conclusion. This is an evidence gap, not an observed failure. Typical cause: No tracking records were provided.
findings.recommendation: Provide the evidence the control requires so it can be concluded. If a gap is then confirmed: Track findings to closure with evidence, and close only after a later check confirms the fix.
findings.closureCriterion: Review of closures made after the correction date.

findings.label: F-05
findings.description: The reviewer concluded the criteria were met only in part over the reviewed sample.
findings.risk: No one accountable for sovereignty decisions.
findings.recommendation: Name accountable owners, document responsibilities, and review the sovereignty posture on a fixed cadence.
findings.closureCriterion: Evidence of the next scheduled review after the correction.

limitations: This is a limited-scope assessment of the declared scope only; conditions outside it were not examined.
Results are point-in-time, as of the evidence cutoff, and do not describe the system before or after it.
Conclusions depend on the evidence made available; most evidence was supplied by the assessed organization and was not independently authenticated.
Every rn.sv control is concluded by an authenticated human reviewer; the conclusions involve professional judgement.
This report is not a certification, accreditation, attestation of compliance, or seal of any kind.
This report is not a legal opinion and does not state compliance with any law or regulation.
This report does not establish the absence of vulnerabilities, and no security testing was performed against the assessed systems.
The score is specific to the rn.sv@0.1.0 framework, its methodology and the declared scope; it is not a general trust or security score.
Document digests show that this report has not changed since it was generated; they do not show that the underlying evidence is true, and they are not a digital signature.

evidenceRequired: SV-03: The policy in force with its version history, plus a sample of decisions taken under it.
SV-06: Tenant-isolation design documentation and the output of isolation tests executed by the customer, witnessed or recorded.
SV-07: A field inventory for the in-scope exports and APIs, plus sample exports or responses.
SV-09: The finding-tracking process and closure evidence for previously identified issues.
SV-10: Named accountable owners, a responsibility matrix, review cadence records, and the escalation path.
invalidatingChanges: Changes to the in-scope systems, their architecture or their tenancy model.
Changes to the authority, consent or revocation mechanisms.
A new policy version or a change in how decisions record the policy applied.
Changes to logging, record integrity or disclosure profiles.
Material incidents affecting the in-scope systems after the evidence cutoff.
revalidation.linkage: A revalidation is a new assessment that references assurance-assessment-1; this assessment and this report are never modified.
revalidation.monitoring: Not included. This report describes one point-in-time assessment; continuous monitoring is a separate service.

commercialUse.statement: The framework definition records commercial use as restricted pending controlled review. Release of this report requires an authenticated human approver to acknowledge that restriction and act as that review; the release record states whether this happened.

integrity.release: Not released by this document. Release is a separate record that binds an authenticated human approval to this report’s digests.
integrity.limitation: The digests in the manifest show integrity only. They are not a digital signature, do not provide non-repudiation, and do not authenticate the evidence.
